resolutions.rationale: Uncertainty need not bar action, but nearby tradition does not follow from generic power.
The higher power's concern and the nearby tradition's access are unsupported assumptions.
It answers doctrinal underdetermination pragmatically but not its metaphysical substance.
The move materially supports practice before certainty, a central pro burden.
The recommended first step is clear, while probably lacks an evidential threshold.
It concedes possible error and argues only against complete suspension of prayer.
Unequal experiences coherently create a challenge, although this move offers no solution.
It candidly identifies a major counterconsideration relevant to religious obligation.
It exposes a burden the pro account must answer rather than presently supporting it.
The difference between intense experience and its absence is stated clearly.
The speaker fairly grants why recipients believe and why others remain unconvinced.
Knowledge of the map does not plainly remove freedom to reject it or act otherwise.
The alleged goods of concealment, differentiated roles, and journey are speculative assertions.
It directly addresses selective revelation but leaves the dilemma's sufficiency horn unanswered.
The move directly addresses hiddenness, a subsidiary burden supporting the pro case.
Freedom, journey, hiddenness, and differentiated roles are invoked without precise mechanisms.
The speaker uses may and probably, although also treats the world as a given.
Expected mystery under hiddenness does not establish that apparently gratuitous suffering has purpose.
No mechanism connects freedom or partial hiddenness to unexplained animal and infant suffering.
It concedes the residue but does not answer the animal-specific or intuition challenge.
The move addresses compatibility, yet offers little probability against gratuitous evil.
Non-gratuity, residue, freedom, and hiddenness are stated, but their relations remain vague.
It candidly admits severe cases that the presented account cannot explain.
A distinct developmental good can answer heaven, but its value sufficient for suffering is assumed.
No support is given that tested souls possess an angel-lacking good worth the suffering.
It directly distinguishes earthly formation from the completed state in heaven.
The reply addresses the counterexample but does not show the value is proportionate.
Progression toward holiness is clear, though what the perfected soul gains is unspecified.
The speaker acknowledges what the view must establish but talks as if that may justify all suffering.
Practice can have value amid uncertainty, but fruits do not establish obligation or truth.
The fruits of worship and prayer are asserted without specification or comparative evidence.
It recommends practice while largely bypassing the objection that doctrinal repairs abandon Christianity.
The move returns directly to practical obligation, though the evidential bridge remains incomplete.
The practices are concrete, while their fruits and cross-theology validity remain vague.
Calling theological difficulties distractions understates their significance to the target objection.
All affirmative burden-completion consequences are already represented in the scored move dimensions, so no distinct adjustment is eligible.
All skeptical burden-completion consequences are already represented in the scored move dimensions, so no distinct adjustment is eligible.
